text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock has climbed 0.69% today and 9.6% over the past two weeks, driven primarily by a sharp rally since mid-September tied to Middle East supply disruptions. Iran has closed the Strait of Hormuz, Saudi Arabia's energy infrastructure has come under attack, and geopolitical tensions have escalated — all of which raise concerns about global oil supply. This backdrop, combined with U.S. crude trading at $107 per barrel and refineries running at 96.8% capacity, supports higher margins for refiners like Marathon, which profit when crude costs rise but they can still move product.

The two-week move also reflects broad market relief that initial fears about Saudi pipeline damage proved less severe than expected, suggesting the market is pricing in elevated but manageable supply risks rather than a catastrophic disruption. With gasoline and diesel inventories relatively lean and refineries already running at near-full tilt, any sustained supply squeeze would further tighten margins in refiners' favor.
